title: Regression exposure
description: What a realized change exposes outside the files it modified: which consumers observe what changed, and what breaks for each. The after to code-inventory's before — a survey's risks are predictions from a plan, and these are consequences of code that exists. `unexposed` is carried alongside `exposures` because a consumer examined and cleared is not the same as one nobody looked at, and only the artifact can tell them apart. No severity: whether a break is acceptable is the caller's.

report_id.description: Supplied by the caller and never minted by the producer.

modified.description: The change as stated, one entry per path. Stated rather than derived from a diff, so the report names the change the caller has in mind.

changed.description: What changed in it, in terms of what is observable from outside.

exposures.description: One entry per consumer that could break, sorted by consumer path. Empty is a real result: the change was traced outward and nothing observes it.

consumer.description: The path that would notice. Importing is not observing: a consumer that never reaches the changed behavior does not belong here.

kind.description: How the change is observable. `removal` breaks at load rather than at a branch, which is why it is found by searching for the name rather than by reading callers.

breaks.description: What goes wrong for this consumer, specifically.

evidence.description: What in the consumer makes it so.

unexposed.description: Consumers examined and cleared, with why. Required so a reader can tell a cleared consumer from an unexamined one.

prior_risks_checked.description: Where a code inventory predicted risks, each one confirmed or dropped. A predicted risk left unmentioned reads as still open.
